title: ～しかない — have no choice but to ～
summary: Says that there is no other way and only one option remains: “have no choice but to ～.” It follows a verb dictionary form. The speaker accepts the situation or firmly decides on that one course.

patterns.gloss: verb dictionary form + しかない (歩くしかない)
noun + しかない: only that is left (これしかない)

body.p: In the pattern しか + negative, it expresses limitation to only that. After a verb it means “there is no other way, so I have to do ～.” It often follows a reason, as in バスがないので、歩くしかない. The polite form is 〜しかありません.

body.h: Compared with ほかない and だけ
body.p: 〜ほかない, 〜よりほかない and 〜ざるを得ない mean similar things, but しかない is the most everyday. だけ limits in the affirmative, while しかない pairs with a negative and stresses that it is little or not enough. It also suggests choosing reluctantly, not willingly.

examples.ja: バスがないので、歩（ある）くしかない。
examples.romaji: Basu ga nai node, aruku shika nai.
examples.tr: There's no bus, so I have no choice but to walk.
examples.note: A reason, then the only option.

examples.ja: 終電（しゅうでん）を逃（のが）したので、タクシーで帰（かえ）るしかない。
examples.romaji: Shūden o nogashita node, takushī de kaeru shika nai.
examples.tr: I missed the last train, so I have no choice but to go home by taxi.

examples.ja: 誰（だれ）も助（たす）けてくれないなら、自分（じぶん）でやるしかない。
examples.romaji: Dare mo tasukete kurenai nara, jibun de yaru shika nai.
examples.tr: If no one will help, I have no choice but to do it myself.

pitfalls: After しか a negative is required: × 歩くしかある. End with ない or ありません.
The verb is the dictionary form: × 歩いたしかない, ○ 歩くしかない.
